content.text:
This is a standard multi-part FRQ-style item (average value, derivative meaning, net change, solving an integral equation), and each part is routine for AP Calculus AB.

Part (a) applies the average value formula: (1/20)∫100e^(-t/5) dt = 5(100)(1 - e^-4)/20 ≈ 24.54. That is one step.

Part (b) is a derivative, F'(t) = -20e^(-t/5), so F'(3) ≈ -10.97. The student then interprets it with units (gal/hr²).

Part (c) is 300 + ∫(F - 25) dt = 300 + 500(1 - e^-4) - 500 ≈ 290.8. That is a calculator integral plus an initial value.

Part (d) sets 300 + ∫0^t (F(s) - 25) ds = 300, so ∫0^t (100e^(-s/5) - 25) ds = 0. The equation is solved on the calculator, which also needs the justification that exactly one such time exists. The solution comes from 500(1 - e^(-t/5)) = 25t, giving t ≈ 13.9.

The numbers are clean and the reading load is modest. The item does ask for justification, mainly in the units and meaning in (b) and the equation setup in (d).

Because it combines several parts and several skills, it fits full-mock use.
